source.title: Large Brain Model for Learning Generic Representations with Tremendous EEG Data in BCI
source.authors: Wei-Bang Jiang; Li-Ming Zhao; Bao-Liang Lu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figures and chart text are garbled in the extracted text.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines scaling in EEG models, a different modality, and reports downstream performance at different model sizes and pre-training data amounts. It does not test the language-model loss or compute-allocation claims directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that larger LaBraM models reach lower pre-training loss in Figure 3 and discusses data-size scaling in Figure 5. Figure 3 does not report held-out loss values or a power-law fit. Figure 5's curves are not numerically readable in the extracted text; the qualitative data-size statements are recorded as aggregate results. The language-model loss and compute-optimal allocation measures are not tested.
record.test_reason: This is an EEG foundation-model method paper (LaBraM). Scaling serves as motivation, and the results are the method's own downstream scores at three sizes (5.8M, 46M, 369M) and several pre-training data amounts. No loss values are given, no power law is fitted, and nothing is extrapolated or allocated by compute. The rows do not measure what any version names. V1-V4 and V6-V7 concern language models. V5 requires the same power-law form, which three unfitted downstream points cannot show. The authors' remark that results 'basically follow the scaling law' is a qualitative citation, not a test. The downstream size trend is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that larger LaBraM models perform better (Huge > Large > Base), attributing this to more pre-training data and parameters. They also find that more pre-training data helps larger models most. They say this 'basically follows the scaling law' of Kaplan et al., without fitting one, and speculate that Huge needs at least ~10,000 hours of data. Their headline conclusion is that LaBraM outperforms prior SOTA EEG methods.
record.recipe_differences: EEG masked-token pre-training and downstream fine-tuning, rather than language-model pre-training evaluated by held-out cross-entropy; no power-law fit or compute-optimal allocation is performed.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that data-size trends vary by model size and downstream task: Base results are non-monotonic on TUAB, Large-model growth slows after 1000 hours, and Huge-model performance trends upward with more data.

fits_no_version.finding: In EEG foundation models, fine-tuned downstream metrics mostly rise from 5.8M to 46M to 369M parameters. Examples: TUAB AUROC 0.9022→0.9127→0.9162; MoBI R2 0.2876→0.3093→0.3145. Gains are tiny or within SD on SEED-V and TUEV, and TUEV Kappa is non-monotone. Data scaling helps the Huge model, saturates after ~1000h for Large, and is non-monotone for Base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream task performance of foundation models in non-text modalities (e.g. EEG) improves with model and pre-training data size, with data benefits growing with model size.

record.problems: The study does not evaluate held-out pre-training loss against model size, data, or compute, and does not fit a power law. The data-size results in Figure 5 are not numerically readable in the supplied extraction; the text summarizes them qualitatively. Model size and architecture dimensions change together, and the downstream comparisons do not establish prediction from pre-training loss.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric data-size curve values are extracted from Figure 5 because the plotted values are not readable in the supplied text; the text's aggregate descriptions are recorded in r37-r40. Figure 3's masked EEG pre-training-loss curves are not included as rows because they are not held-out language-model cross-entropy measurements and report no power-law fit.

untested.parts: No held-out LM loss and no power-law fit. Figure 3 pre-training loss curves are EEG masked-token loss, not held-out, and have no fit.
Depth and width change together with parameter count; shape is not varied at fixed size.
EEG is a new modality, but there is no loss-vs-scale power-law fit. Only three sizes and qualitative data-size curves are given.
No LM downstream results. The EEG downstream trends with size are not fitted or predicted from loss.
No fitting choices or exponents compared.

record.verdict_notes: I demoted the reader's 'tests/T3' with V6 supports and limits_scope labels. V6 concerns language-model downstream predictability, and the paper fits no scaling law, so no version verdicts are given. The paper calls Table 6 'Figure 6' in its text. Figure 3 loss curves and Figure 5 values are unreadable in the extraction. The record's rows_left_out already declares them.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model cross-entropy loss is measured, and no power-law fit is reported.
No small-run fit is extrapolated to larger language-model runs.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation is tested.
Depth and width are changed along with model size; the study does not isolate architecture effects at fixed parameter count.
The study uses EEG, but it does not measure whether a held-out loss follows the same power-law form in another modality or training regime.
The study reports downstream EEG task metrics across model sizes and pre-training data amounts, but does not test whether downstream performance is predicted from pre-training loss.
The study does not compare fitting choices or report changes in fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: LaBraM-Base
rows.operation_detail: Compare downstream metrics across LaBraM model sizes.
rows.note: The score is lower than the Large and Huge model scores.
rows.check: These are fine-tuned downstream metrics of EEG models at three sizes, not language-model results, so they cannot bear on V6. No power-law fit is reported, so they cannot show V5's power-law form. Several size gaps are within the reported SD (e.g. SEED-V accuracy 0.4095±0.0062 vs 0.4096±0.0075 vs 0.4102±0.0037; TUEV Weighted F1 0.8312 vs 0.8315 vs 0.8329, SD up to 0.0086). So 'observed' monotone improvement is overstated for SEED-V and TUEV. r13-r14 (TUEV Kappa) are non-monotone: Large 0.6622 is below Base 0.6637, within error.
